HX1.sql_query:
WITH MonthlySales AS (
    SELECT 
        o.customer_id, 
        DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date) AS month, 
        SUM(o.freight) AS monthly_revenue
    FROM public.orders o
    GROUP BY o.customer_id, DATE_TRUNC('month', o.order_date)
),
FirstLastMonthRevenue AS (
    SELECT 
        ms.customer_id,
        MIN(ms.month) AS first_month,
        MAX(ms.month) AS last_month,
        FIRST_VALUE(ms.monthly_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.customer_id ORDER BY ms.month) AS first_month_revenue,
        LAST_VALUE(ms.monthly_revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY ms.customer_id ORDER BY ms.month ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND UNBOUNDED FOLLOWING) AS last_month_revenue,
        COUNT(DISTINCT ms.month) AS active_months
    FROM MonthlySales ms
    GROUP BY ms.customer_id, ms.month, ms.monthly_revenue
)
SELECT 
    c.customer_id, 
    c.company_name, 
    flmr.first_month_revenue, 
    flmr.last_month_revenue, 
    (flmr.last_month_revenue - flmr.first_month_revenue) AS revenue_growth
FROM FirstLastMonthRevenue flmr
JOIN public.customers c ON c.customer_id = flmr.customer_id
WHERE flmr.active_months >= 5
ORDER BY revenue_growth DESC
LIMIT 5;

WITH RegionOrderSummary AS (
    SELECT 
        o.ship_region AS region,
        COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count,
        SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS total_revenue
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id

MedianOrderCount AS (
    SELECT PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY order_count) AS median_order_count

FROM RegionOrderSummary ros
JOIN MedianOrderCount moc ON 1=1
WHERE ros.order_count < moc.median_order_count
ORDER BY ros.total_revenue DESC;

HX7.question: Welche Produktpaare aus unterschiedlichen Kategorien werden ueberproportional oft gemeinsam gekauft (Lift gegenueber Unabhaengigkeit)?
HX7.final_response_text:
Hier sind die Top 10 Produktpaare aus unterschiedlichen Kategorien, die überproportional oft gemeinsam gekauft werden, basierend auf ihrem Lift-Wert:

1. Produkt 9 und Produkt 73 mit einem Lift von 0.0286
2. Produkt 9 und Produkt 27 mit einem Lift von 0.0222
3. Produkt 5 und Produkt 9 mit einem Lift von 0.0200
4. Produkt 43 und Produkt 48 mit einem Lift von 0.0119
5. Produkt 6 und Produkt 14 mit einem Lift von 0.0114
6. Produkt 27 und Produkt 67 mit einem Lift von 0.0111
7. Produkt 8 und Produkt 12 mit einem Lift von 0.0110
8. Produkt 20 und Produkt 37 mit einem Lift von 0.0104
9. Produkt 5 und Produkt 29 mit einem Lift von 0.0094
10. Produkt 15 und Produkt 25 mit einem Lift von 0.0093

Diese Paare zeigen eine höhere Wahrscheinlichkeit, gemeinsam gekauft zu werden, als es bei unabhängigen Käufen der Fall wäre.
HX7.sql_query:
WITH product_pairs AS (
  SELECT 
    od1.product_id AS product_id1, 
    od2.product_id AS product_id2, 
    COUNT(*) AS pair_count
  FROM 
    public.order_details od1
  JOIN 
    public.order_details od2 ON od1.order_id = od2.order_id AND od1.product_id < od2.product_id
  JOIN 
    public.products p1 ON od1.product_id = p1.product_id
  JOIN 
    public.products p2 ON od2.product_id = p2.product_id
  WHERE 
    p1.category_id <> p2.category_id
  GROUP BY 
    od1.product_id, od2.product_id
),
product_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    product_id, 
    COUNT(*) AS total_count
  FROM 
    public.order_details
  GROUP BY 
    product_id
)
SELECT 
  pp.product_id1, 
  pp.product_id2, 
  pp.pair_count, 
  pt1.total_count AS total_count1, 
  pt2.total_count AS total_count2,
  (pp.pair_count::float / (pt1.total_count * pt2.total_count)) AS lift
FROM 
  product_pairs pp
JOIN 
  product_totals pt1 ON pp.product_id1 = pt1.product_id
JOIN 
  product_totals pt2 ON pp.product_id2 = pt2.product_id
ORDER BY 
  lift DESC
LIMIT 10;

HX13.question: Welche Mitarbeitenden dominieren einzelne Regionen stark (Anteil groesser als 50 Prozent des Regionalumsatzes)?
HX13.final_response_text: Es gibt keine Mitarbeitenden, die mehr als 50% des Umsatzes in einer einzelnen Region dominieren. Wenn du weitere Analysen benötigst oder andere Fragen hast, lass es mich wissen!
HX13.sql_query:
WITH regional_sales AS (
    SELECT r.region_id, r.region_description, e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name,
           SUM(od.unit_price * od.quantity * (1 - od.discount)) AS employee_sales
    FROM public.orders o
    JOIN public.order_details od ON o.order_id = od.order_id
    JOIN public.employees e ON o.employee_id = e.employee_id
    JOIN public.territories t ON o.ship_region = t.territory_id
    JOIN public.region r ON t.region_id = r.region_id
    GROUP BY r.region_id, r.region_description, e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name
),
region_totals AS (
    SELECT region_id, SUM(employee_sales) AS total_sales
    FROM regional_sales
    GROUP BY region_id
)
SELECT rs.employee_id, rs.first_name, rs.last_name, rs.region_description, rs.employee_sales, rt.total_sales
FROM regional_sales rs
JOIN region_totals rt ON rs.region_id = rt.region_id
WHERE rs.employee_sales > 0.5 * rt.total_sales;
